title: The Murdered Famous Detective
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Yokomizo) omitted by convention, matching the ep011 precedent of omitting Megure. The old wiki-derived case file (cases/ep185-186_the_murdered_famous_detective.json) had the right culprit (Tahara) but flattened the mechanism into two generic objects/events and missed most of the cast and structure: it omitted victim Sunaoka's actual death mechanism (a bowgun-fired, screw-threaded bullet fashioned to mimic rifle rifling, not simply 'a bullet extracted from a test mattress' fired from a crossbow at range), omitted lodge owner Akashi entirely, omitted the red-herring motives against Nagatsuka (embezzlement accusation) and Tanigawa (agency-switch threat + romantic-humiliation jab), omitted Tanigawa's archery near-miss (a plausible weapon-skill red herring given the real weapon turns out to be a bow), omitted the recorded-dialogue phone trick and firecracker used to fake the time/location of the shooting, and omitted the shoe-glass and coconut-fiber clues that actually break the case. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved, sharing an `order` integer so edges from the same real-world occurrence group without a reifying node. case_type: murder.

persons.name: Kazuyoshi Sunaoka
persons.occupation: actor (age 30), plays detective character 'Urban Hunter / Sabao Banai' in a TV series

attrs.died_of: pierced through the forehead by a bowgun bolt tipped with a modified bullet, staged to look like a long-range rifle shot
attrs.personality: arrogant toward the crew; publicly humiliates producer, scriptwriter, and manager at dinner

attrs.accused_of: pocketing part of the production budget (accusation made publicly by Sunaoka at dinner; denies it)
attrs.alibi: took a long-distance phone call from Tokyo/the station at the lodge's private corded front-desk phone right around the time of the fake gunshot; confirmed by the caller and phone records

persons.name: Noe Tanigawa
persons.occupation: owner/CEO of Sunaoka's talent management agency, age 27

attrs.accused_of: possible romantic grudge (needled by Nagatsuka at dinner about being 'dumped')
attrs.skill: practices archery; nearly struck a stranger with a stray arrow at the lodge's archery ground earlier that day -- a red herring given the real murder weapon turns out to be a bow
attrs.alibi_gap: no witness for the time right after the gunshot was heard (was showering, then came out to the veranda alone) -- moot, since the true time of death was earlier

persons.name: Toshiaki Tahara
persons.occupation: scenario writer for Sunaoka's TV series, age 35

attrs.claimed_alibi: said he stayed in his room all afternoon writing, then went to the garden restaurant kitchen for more drinks around 7:50pm
attrs.true_activity: spent the afternoon secretly stealing a rifle and rope, faking a sniper scene across the valley, and manufacturing a fake bullet-tipped arrow; killed Sunaoka around 7:50pm and faked a call and gunshot around 8:00pm
attrs.confession: wanted to prove -- to the producers, the actor, the police, and even the most famous detective -- that he could commit a perfect, unsolvable crime, after being mocked and blamed for bad ratings by Sunaoka

persons.name: Yusaku Akashi
persons.occupation: owner/innkeeper of the mountain lodge, age 60

attrs.alibi: was alone, washing dishes in the kitchen with the ventilation fan running at the time of the fake gunshot; ruled out early since he is lodge staff, not one of the three guests who could have needed a false alibi

attrs.description: secluded lodge accessible by a single mountain road, run alone by Akashi
site staged to look like the sniper's position; about a 30-minute round trip from the lodge, visible from the garden restaurant

attrs.floor_marks: scratches/drag marks on the floor from moving the heavy bowgun in and out, noticed by Conan

attrs.description: source of the rifle and rope later found staged on the cliff

objects.name: Rifle (stolen from the hunting management office)

attrs.staging_flaw: underside found dry despite the evening rain -- proves it was planted on the cliff before the rain, hours earlier than the claimed 8:00pm shooting
attrs.purpose: used once, in secret, to fire a test bullet into the mattress propped at Sunaoka's window so a bullet bearing the rifle's rifling marks would exist; then left on the cliff as a decoy

objects.name: Rope (stolen from the hunting management office)

attrs.purpose: tied to a tree on the cliff to fake a rope-and-boat escape route down to the stream
used to catch the test bullet fired by the rifle without a body present, and to break the window glass realistically
attrs.material: coconut-fiber stuffing, later found mixed into the glass shards at the scene

objects.name: Modified bullet (test-fired into the mattress, then drilled and sharpened)

attrs.origin: fired from rifle o1 into mattress o3 to acquire a bullet with matching rifling marks
attrs.modification: a screw-threaded hole drilled into its base and its tip filed to a point, so it could be screwed onto an arrow shaft as a makeshift arrowhead
attrs.recovered_from: Sunaoka's forehead wound, extracted during autopsy
attrs.anomaly: forensics flagged the drilled screw threads as inexplicable on a rifle bullet -- the detail that tips Conan off

attrs.found: hidden in Tahara's room 304 during a police search ordered after Conan's tip
hidden alongside the bowgun in room 304
attrs.match: screw threads on the tip match the drilled modification on the bullet recovered from the body

attrs.purpose: thrown toward the valley around 8:00pm to fake the sound of the sniper's gunshot and its apparent distant location/timing

objects.name: Recorded playback of Sunaoka's own TV-show dialogue

attrs.line: "How about it? Why don't you come up to my room and we'll talk detective?" ... "Huh? Hold on a second, what is that?"
attrs.purpose: played over the phone to Kogoro Mouri to impersonate a still-alive Sunaoka and fake an interrupted call, planting a false, later time of death

attrs.handed_out: at dinner, giving Tahara Kogoro's phone number for the faked call

attrs.purpose: drawn to hide the broken window hole after cleanup, then reopened later to stage the final scene

clues.desc: The glass shards collected from Sunaoka's broken window were mixed with coconut/plant fibers that don't belong to window glass but match the stuffing of the room's mattress -- proving a mattress had been used to catch a test bullet fired through the window, rather than the window simply having been shot out from across the valley.

Shards of glass matching the crime-scene window were found stuck in the sole of Tahara's shoe, even though only investigators approached the body after the scene was found -- meaning Tahara must have been in the room around the broken glass earlier, while gathering it up as part of staging the scene, before the police 'discovery.'

The rifle staged on the cliff was dry underneath despite the evening rain that soaked everything else at the scene, while the timeline claimed it was left there around 8:00pm (after the rain had already stopped) -- the dryness only makes sense if the rifle was actually planted hours earlier, in the afternoon, before the rain.

No footprints were found on either side of the mountain road/bridge crossing to the cliff, even though everyone had to cross it after the rain -- ruling out any outsider physically walking to or from the sniper position, and undermining the entire across-the-valley sniper narrative.

edges.detail: the famous-detective TV drama's cast and crew are all staying together at the secluded mountain lodge for filming
Akashi runs the lodge alone
takes a long-distance call from Tokyo on the lodge's private corded front-desk phone around the time of the fake gunshot, giving him his alibi
loosed a stray arrow at the archery ground that nearly struck a passerby, establishing her as bow-skilled ahead of the reveal that the real weapon is a bowgun
props the mattress against Sunaoka's window as a bullet catcher
fires the stolen rifle at Sunaoka's empty room from across the valley, lodging a bullet in the propped mattress
leaves the rifle on the cliff as a decoy
ties the rope to a tree to fake a rope-and-boat escape route
retrieves the fired bullet from the mattress
cleans up the broken glass and draws the curtain to hide the hole after restoring the mattress
drills screw threads into the base and sharpens the tip
screws the modified bullet onto an arrow shaft, loaded into the bowgun
publicly accuses Nagatsuka of pocketing production budget money
mocks Tahara's scripts and blames him for falling ratings
threatens to leave her agency for a rival production company that offered him a bigger contract
needles Tanigawa about a rumored breakup in front of everyone
walks Sunaoka back to his room, then leaves for her own room to shower
sneaks in under the pretense of getting more drinks

edges.method: pierced through the forehead at close range with a bowgun-fired arrow tipped with the rifle-marked, screw-threaded bullet

edges.detail: repositions the body to face the window, reopens the curtain, rescatters the pre-collected glass shards, and removes the arrow shaft, leaving only the bullet-shaped tip embedded to mimic a gunshot wound
returns to the garden restaurant acting normal, deliberately sitting apart from the group
secretly calls Kogoro Mouri and plays a recording of Sunaoka's own TV dialogue to fake a still-alive Sunaoka and an interrupted call
got Kogoro's phone number off the business card handed out at dinner
throws a firecracker toward the valley to fake the sound, timing, and apparent location of the gunshot
investigators and Mouri's party cross the 30-minute route to the cliff after the fake gunshot is heard, find the rifle and rope staged there

edges.motive_type: professional/artistic pride -- mocked and blamed for bad ratings, wanted to prove he could commit a perfect, unsolvable crime that would fool everyone including the police and the most famous detective
financial (publicly, humiliatingly accused of embezzling production budget) -- red herring
professional and personal (his threat to switch agencies would ruin her business; also publicly needled about a romantic breakup) -- red herring
